reusable_cues.rationale: Agreement-against-hand-tags is a reusable cue for evaluating a tagger against a human reference set.

source_text:
## Acceptance checklist (2026-09-30)

- [ ] Mark 3 tags arXiv papers using an arXiv-aware prompt and hierarchical pattern set, with batch coverage and hand-tagging agreement measured and recorded.
- [ ] Mark 3 uses eprint input by default for rich theorem-and-proof hypergraphs.
- [ ] Mark 3 reverse-morphogenesis output records failures explicitly instead of null analyses and rejects collapsed situation, salience, and constraint slots.
- [ ] Mark 3 emits geometry artifacts with tension, unpaired claims, and hypergraph Laplacian summaries for papers and batches.
- [ ] Mark 3 passes the inherited Mark 2 regression checks and uses a separate manifest with a tested rollback to Mark 2.

sentences.unresolved_reason: Heading only; names the checklist and date, carries no interpretable move.

fragments.text: Mark 3 tags arXiv papers using an arXiv-aware prompt and hierarchical pattern set
fragments.target: arXiv papers, tagged by Mark 3 with a domain-aware prompt and a fixed hierarchical pattern vocabulary
fragments.rationale: The deliverable is an automated tagger whose labels are constrained to a curated hierarchical pattern set rather than free description; the arXiv-aware prompt supplies the domain framing.

pattern_refs.rationale: Tagging papers with a fixed hierarchical pattern set is exactly constraining an extracted field to the downstream vocabulary so the consumer gets operation names, not paraphrase.

pattern_rejections.reason: That pattern classifies hygiene items by how much judgement their remedy needs; this item tags papers against a domain taxonomy, where the axis is subject-matter patterns, not remedy cost.
pattern_rejections.query: classify items with a domain-aware prompt and a hierarchical tag set

pattern_rejections.reason: Smoke-testing a prompt on a held-out sample is a cost-control step before a paid run; the acceptance item specifies the tagger itself and its measured quality, not a pre-run cost gate.
pattern_rejections.query: classify items with a domain-aware prompt and a hierarchical tag set

fragments.target: tagging quality, measured as batch coverage plus agreement against human hand-tagging
fragments.rationale: Acceptance requires the tagger to be scored against a human reference: agreement with hand-tagging presupposes a hand-verified comparison set, and coverage quantifies how much of the batch gets tagged.

pattern_refs.rationale: Hand-tagging agreement is only meaningful against a curated, hand-verified reference set rather than raw pipeline output, which is what this pattern mandates.

pattern_rejections.reason: That pattern selects where to measure by uncertainty; this item fixes the metric in advance (coverage and hand-tag agreement) rather than choosing measurement sites adaptively.
pattern_rejections.query: measure agreement between machine labels and human hand-tagging

fragments.target: the coverage and agreement numbers, which must be recorded with their derivation
fragments.rationale: The item does not accept informal claims of quality: the metrics must be recorded so the acceptance claim is checkable later, which is a provenance requirement on the numbers.

pattern_refs.rationale: Requiring the metrics to be measured and recorded makes the acceptance claim checkable rather than asserted, exactly the warrant-travels-with-the-number discipline.
